svg.title: Neonatal sepsis by age of onset (single colour)
svg.desc: Early-onset sepsis, in the first 72 hours, comes from the mother around birth: usually group B streptococcus, Escherichia coli or Listeria monocytogenes. Late-onset sepsis, after 72 hours, is linked to central lines, devices and the neonatal unit, especially in preterm babies: usually coagulase-negative staphylococci or Staphylococcus aureus, Gram-negative bacilli such as Klebsiella and E. coli, or Candida.
svg.text: Early onset (first 72 hours): from the mother around birth
Late onset (after 72 hours): from lines, devices and the neonatal unit
